review_record: owner authorization given in the Claude Code session that prepared this change; no separate reviewer record was produced
approval_basis: Owner-authorized successor admitting one Metal instruction contract, metal.precise.tanh.f32, on apple_gpu_family7 and apple_gpu_family8. This approval was written by the author session at the owner's explicit instruction; no independent reviewer session inspected the change, so it does not carry the independent-review basis of approvals made under ADR 0052 by a distinct session. What it repairs: v68 mapped ElementwiseOp.TANH to precise::tanh and the Metal backend's refusal text advertised tanh, but the IR requires tanh to name an instruction contract, both Apple Targets admitted none, and the backend refused every contract unconditionally. tanh was therefore unreachable from any Apple Schedule and that mapping was dead. Adding an activation task family (SiLU, SwiGLU, GELU-tanh) reached the gap on its first authored GELU starter. The contract is named rather than implied because precise::tanh and fast::tanh are different functions with different cost, which is the same reason libdevice.tanh.f32 is named on the CUDA targets. The Metal backend still refuses every other contract, PTX FMA included. What the author session verified: the Corpus Gate was rebuilt from source and matched 124/124 cases over 171 bound sources for draft open-cake-ir-sm100a-v71-draft, with every expectation unchanged and no corpus file edited, so no existing lowering was altered; and the GELU starter now lowers to precise::tanh and matches its independent oracle on all five required input cases in the portable CPU semantic shim. No device measurement of tanh was taken on any Apple target, so no performance claim is approved here, and no PTX RN equivalence is implied for Metal rounding. This approves the Compiler successor only; it approves no Executor release, no framework acceptance and no scientific arm comparison.
